description: russia-colonialism techniques used by Integration Reforms of Peter I and the Great Northern War (1700–1708), ATT&CK campaign C0011 (v1.3)
name: Integration Reforms of Peter I and the Great Northern War (1700–1708) (C0011)

techniques.comment: Preparation for the liquidation of the Hetmanate through the gubernia reform, into which Cossack towns were artificially inscribed. Moscow planned "to take the Little Russian towns into its own domain"(Citation: Иван Мазепа и Российская империя. История «предательства» 2011)(Citation: Мазепа 2007).

A course toward the complete absorption and destruction of the very name of the Cossack state. In the Bendery Constitution of 1710, Orlyk recorded Moscow's intention "to eradicate the Zaporozhian Host of the Lower Dnipro and to efface its name forever"(Citation: Иван Мазепа и Российская империя. История «предательства» 2011). Hrushevsky confirms the course was systemic: Mazepa's alliance with the Swedish king merely "gave the Muscovite government occasion… to take up more forcefully the abolition of Ukrainian autonomy. The Muscovite government had pursued this line from the very beginning"(Citation: Ілюстрована історія України 1921). What was at stake was the enslavement of the entire people: the Muscovite state, per the preamble of Orlyk's constitution, managed to "violate and utterly destroy" the rights and liberties "and to cast a slave's yoke upon the free Cossack people, never conquered by it"(Citation: Договори і постанови прав і свобод військових (Конституція Пилипа Орлика) 1710).

The dispatch of Cossack regiments to distant theaters of war (the Baltic lands, Poland), which led to their exhaustion. The troops were "wearied by year-round military service, impoverished, dismounted, destitute"(Citation: Иван Мазепа и Российская империя. История «предательства» 2011)(Citation: Мазепа 2007).

The strangulation of the autonomy's economy through the system of billeting the regular army: "And when the kompaniytsi and serdiuks stand in winter quarters... 24 commoners feed a single kompaniyets without any excuses"(Citation: Иван Мазепа и Российская империя. История «предательства» 2011)(Citation: Мазепа 2007).

The mass conscription of the population for the construction of military installations in Moscow's interests. The tsar officially thanked the hetman and the starshyna for their "diligent zeal (and considerable labors borne) in the making of the Pechersk fortification" and promised for this "service and labors in the making of the said fortification" his "most exalted favor"(Citation: Иван Мазепа и Российская империя. История «предательства» 2011).

Preparation for dismantling the autonomy during the reforms of 1707: by Orlyk's account, the Cossack starshyna expected the empire to be preparing "to turn the Cossacks into a regular army… to break the rights and liberties of the Host"(Citation: Иван Мазепа и Российская империя. История «предательства» 2011)(Citation: Мазепа 2007).
